arc — ANNOTATE shape op

• Data kinds: image2d → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.arc(img, center, radius, start_deg, end_deg, color='neutral', width=2, alpha=1.0, scheme='okabe_ito') (to call the implementation directly, import annotate; annotate.arc(img, center, radius, start_deg, end_deg, color='neutral', width=2, alpha=1.0, scheme='okabe_ito'); from the registry, opsannotate.get("arc"))

Usage

A circular arc. Angles are in degrees, clockwise from the screen x-axis (because row points down).

Raises

ValueError

radius not positive, angle non-finite, start == end, alpha outside [0,1].

Drawing: paints pixels whose distance d from the centre satisfies |d - radius| <= max(0.6, width/2) and whose azimuth lies in the range (end_deg - start_deg) mod 360 clockwise from start_deg (no anti-aliasing). The azimuth is atan2(y - cy, x - cx), with 0 degrees = right (+x), 90 degrees = down (+y), clockwise positive.

• center: (x, y), x = column, y = row. May be outside the image (overhang is simply cut off).

• radius: positive [px].

• start_deg, end_deg: degrees. Drawn clockwise from start to end. A difference that is a multiple of 360 (end - start not 0 but e.g. 360) is a full circle. start == end is "length 0", hence ValueError.

• width: line width [px]. max(0.6, width/2) is used as the half-width, so even below 1 px it does not break up.

• img / color / alpha / scheme are handled as in rounded_rect (float64 copy, [0, 1], role name or RGB).

• Return value: float64 of the same shape as the input.

For the conventions of academic figures that write angles in, annotate_angle takes care of everything down to the leader text.
